```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.4,
                      dpi = 150, fig.align = "center")
pal <- c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#009E73", "#CC79A7", "#E69F00", "#56B4E9")
par_default <- function(...) par(mar = c(4.2, 4.2, 1, 1), las = 1, bty = "l",
                                 cex.axis = 0.9, ...)

# The results live in the repository, not in the installed package: find them.
find_root <- function() {
  d <- normalizePath(getwd())
  for (i in 1:6) {
    if (file.exists(file.path(d, "results", "compute_article_numbers.json")))
      return(d)
    d <- dirname(d)
  }
  stop("results/ not found: build this site from the hierarchical-depth repository")
}
root <- find_root()
read_result <- function(name)
  jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(root, "results", paste0(name, ".json")),
                     simplifyVector = FALSE)

# The figures are copied next to this file by `make site` (from figures/ in the
# repository) and referenced by relative path, so pkgdown copies them to the site.
figure <- function(file, caption, width = 100) {
  stopifnot(file.exists(file.path("figures", file)))
  knitr::asis_output(sprintf("\n![%s](figures/%s){width=%d%%}\n\n", caption, file, width))
}
# Two half-width panels side by side (one column each on wide screens).
figure_pair <- function(file1, caption1, file2, caption2) {
  stopifnot(file.exists(file.path("figures", c(file1, file2))))
  knitr::asis_output(sprintf(paste0(
    "\n:::: {.row}\n::: {.col-md-6}\n![%s](figures/%s){width=100%%}\n:::\n",
    "::: {.col-md-6}\n![%s](figures/%s){width=100%%}\n:::\n::::\n\n"),
    caption1, file1, caption2, file2))
}
interval <- function(lo, hi, d = 3)
  sprintf('<span style="white-space:nowrap">%s&ndash;%s</span>', signif(lo, d), signif(hi, d))
pval <- function(p, n_boot) if (p < 1 / n_boot) sprintf("&lt;%g", 1 / n_boot) else sprintf("%.3f", p)
class_label <- function(s) ifelse(s == "0.5", "1/2", "1")
```

main table { font-size: 0.82em; display: block; max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; }

This page collects the numerical results of the accompanying manuscript (in
preparation). The numbers are read from `results/*.json` and the figures from
`figures/` in the [repository](https://github.com/Raydonal/hierarchical-depth).
Both are produced by the Python pipeline of the repository with fixed seeds
(`make results figures`, about 13 minutes). `htheoryR` implements the same
estimators; [Recovering the depth of a cascade](identifiability.html) runs
them in R on simulated data.

## Simulation: size and power of the depth test

```{r power-data}
num <- read_result("compute_article_numbers")
pb <- num$power_by_depth
sizes <- unlist(pb$sample_sizes)
depths <- names(pb$by_N_true)
rate <- sapply(depths, function(N) sapply(as.character(sizes),
               function(n) pb$by_N_true[[N]][[n]]$rate))
se <- sapply(depths, function(N) sapply(as.character(sizes),
             function(n) pb$by_N_true[[N]][[n]]$se))
reps <- pb$by_N_true[[1]][[1]]$n_reps
```

The bootstrap test of $H_0\colon N = `r pb$N0`$ was applied to samples from
cascades of depth $N_{\text{true}} \in \{`r paste(depths, collapse = ", ")`\}$
(class $s = 1/2$, $a = `r pb$a`$), with `r reps` samples per cell and
`r pb$n_boot` bootstrap replicates per test. The row $N_{\text{true}} = 1$ is
the size of the test (nominal level 0.05); the other rows are its power.

```{r power-table}
tab <- data.frame(N_true = depths, t(sapply(depths, function(N)
  sprintf("%.2f (%.3f)", rate[, N], se[, N]))), check.names = FALSE)
names(tab) <- c("True depth", paste("n =", sizes))
knitr::kable(tab, align = "c", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Rejection rate of H0: N = 1 (Monte Carlo standard error).")
```

```{r power-plot, fig.cap = "Rejection rate of the test of H0: N = 1 against the sample size, by true depth, read from results/compute_article_numbers.json. Bars are +/- 1.96 Monte Carlo standard errors; the dashed line is the nominal level 0.05."}
par_default()
plot(NULL, xlim = range(sizes), ylim = c(0, 1), log = "x",
     xlab = "sample size n", ylab = "rejection rate")
abline(h = 0.05, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
for (j in seq_along(depths)) {
  x <- sizes * (1 + 0.04 * (j - 2.5))
  ok <- se[, j] > 0  # a rate of exactly 0 or 1 has no Monte Carlo error bar
  arrows(x[ok], pmax(rate[ok, j] - 1.96 * se[ok, j], 0), x[ok],
         pmin(rate[ok, j] + 1.96 * se[ok, j], 1),
         angle = 90, code = 3, length = 0.03, col = pal[j])
  lines(x, rate[, j], col = pal[j], lwd = 2, lty = j, type = "b", pch = 14 + j)
}
legend("right", bty = "n", col = pal[seq_along(depths)], lty = seq_along(depths),
       pch = 14 + seq_along(depths), lwd = 2,
       legend = paste("true N =", depths))
```

The closed-form log-cumulants were checked against a large sample of an
unequal-shape cascade ($a = (`r paste(unlist(num$cumulant_check$a), collapse = ", ")`)$,
$n = `r format(num$cumulant_check$n, big.mark = ",")`$):

```{r cumulants}
cc <- num$cumulant_check
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  cumulant = paste0("kappa_", seq_along(cc$theory) + 1),
  simulated = unlist(cc$empirical), closed_form = unlist(cc$theory)),
  digits = 4, align = "lrr")
```

```{r fig3}
figure("fig3_identifiability.png", paste(
  "<b>Figure 3.</b> (a) Absolute log-cumulant ratio &kappa;<sub>3</sub>/&kappa;<sub>2</sub>",
  "against the homogeneous shape a; the ratio is negative for s = 1/2 and",
  "positive for s = 1, and for s = 1 it is bounded by 2&zeta;(3)/&zeta;(2) &asymp; 1.46.",
  "(b) The rejection rates of the table above, as in the manuscript."))
```

## Data sets

```{r topology}
topo <- read_result("network_topology")$networks
tt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(topo), function(nm) with(topo[[nm]], data.frame(
  Network = nm, Vertices = n_nodes, Edges = n_edges_undirected,
  Density = format(signif(density, 3)), `Mean degree` = round(mean_degree, 1),
  Transitivity = round(global_clustering, 3),
  Assortativity = round(degree_assortativity, 4), check.names = FALSE))))
knitr::kable(tt, align = "lrrrrrr",
             caption = paste("Descriptive statistics of the three networks as simple",
                             "undirected graphs (isolated vertices removed)."))
```

- **email-Eu-core** ([SNAP](https://snap.stanford.edu/data/email-Eu-core.html)):
  e-mail exchanges in a European research institution. The degree analysis
  keeps all 1005 vertices of the directed graph, including those of degree
  zero.
- **OpenFlights** ([OpenFlights](https://github.com/jpatokal/openflights)):
  airports and the routes between them.
- ***C. elegans*** ([WormAtlas](https://www.wormatlas.org/)): the
  hermaphrodite connectome; chemical synapses and gap junctions, each gap
  junction counted once.
- **Turbulence** ([Mendeley Data](https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/xy8ggx9hn6/1)):
  hot-wire velocity in the wake of a 50 mm cylinder, Re = 5.17 × 10<sup>4</sup>,
  sampled at 1000 Hz, 2<sup>17</sup> values. The analysis uses squared velocity
  increments at lags of 2 to 100 ms.

```{r fig5a}
figure("fig5a_openflights.png", paste(
  "<b>Figure 5a.</b> OpenFlights: airports at their geographic position,",
  "colored by continent, with a random sample of 6000 routes."))
```

```{r fig5bc}
figure_pair("fig5b_email.png", paste(
  "<b>Figure 5b.</b> email-Eu-core adjacency matrix, vertices sorted by",
  "department; pairs within the same department (42 blocks) are shaded."),
  "fig5c_celegans.png", paste(
  "<b>Figure 5c.</b> <i>C. elegans</i> adjacency matrix, neurons sorted by",
  "total degree; chemical synapses in black and gap junctions in orange.",
  "The estimator uses only the degree sequences of the three networks."))
```

## Estimates for the networks

```{r networks-data}
series_table <- function(name, system) {
  d <- read_result(name)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(d$series, function(s) {
    c1 <- s$classes[[s$selected_class]]
    data.frame(System = system, Series = s$series, n = s$n,
               VMR = format(signif(s$vmr, 3)), s = class_label(s$selected_class),
               a_hat = c1$a_hat, a_lo = c1$ci_a_hat[[1]], a_hi = c1$ci_a_hat[[2]],
               N_hat = c1$N_hat, N_lo = c1$ci_N_hat[[1]], N_hi = c1$ci_N_hat[[2]],
               N_round = c1$N_round, p = c1$p_value, n_boot = c1$n_boot,
               lag = if (is.null(s$lag_ms)) NA else s$lag_ms,
               variant = if (is.null(s$variant)) NA else s$variant)
  }))
}
net <- rbind(series_table("analyze_email_eu_core", "email-Eu-core"),
             series_table("analyze_openflights", "OpenFlights"),
             series_table("analyze_celegans", "C. elegans"))
net$Series <- sub("-degree", "", net$Series)
show_table <- function(x, first)
  data.frame(x[first],
             s = x$s,
             `&acirc;` = as.character(signif(x$a_hat, 3)), `95% CI (a)` = interval(x$a_lo, x$a_hi),
             `N&#770;` = as.character(signif(x$N_hat, 3)), `95% CI (N)` = interval(x$N_lo, x$N_hi),
             `N rd` = x$N_round,
             p = mapply(pval, x$p, x$n_boot), check.names = FALSE)
```

For each degree series, only one class is admissible (the sign of the
log-cumulant ratio of the mixing law excludes the other). The table gives the
point estimates of $a$ and $N$ with 95% percentile intervals from 1000
bootstrap resamples of the vertices, the rounded depth $N_{\text{rd}}$, and the
$p$-value of the bootstrap test of $H_0\colon N = N_{\text{rd}}$. Because
$N_{\text{rd}}$ is chosen from the same data, that $p$-value is a
goodness-of-fit diagnostic, not a confirmation of the depth.

```{r networks-table}
knitr::kable(show_table(net, c("System", "Series", "n", "VMR")), escape = FALSE,
             align = "llrrcrlrlcr", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r forest, fig.height = 4.8, fig.cap = "Depth estimates with 95% bootstrap intervals for the nine degree series (logarithmic axis), read from results/analyze_*.json. The dashed line marks N = 1."}
par_default(mar = c(4.2, 13, 1, 1))
y <- rev(seq_len(nrow(net)))
cols <- pal[match(net$System, unique(net$System))]
plot(net$N_hat, y, log = "x", xlim = range(c(net$N_lo, net$N_hi)), yaxt = "n",
     pch = 15 + match(net$System, unique(net$System)), col = cols,
     xlab = expression(hat(N)~"(95% interval)"), ylab = "")
segments(net$N_lo, y, net$N_hi, y, col = cols, lwd = 2)
abline(v = 1, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
axis(2, at = y, labels = paste(net$System, net$Series, "degree"), cex.axis = 0.85)
```

- **email-Eu-core and OpenFlights.** Every series selects $s = 1/2$ with
  $N_{\text{rd}} = 1$, and every interval for $N$ contains one: a single
  gamma mixing level, that is, negative-binomial degrees, describes both
  networks. A single level is a description of the degree law, not evidence of
  a one-level hierarchy.
- ***C. elegans.*** The three series disagree (different rounded depths, and
  the total degree selects the other class), and the intervals are wide. With
  about 250 to 280 neurons, the data do not determine the depth.

```{r fig6abc}
figure_pair("fig6a_email_fit.png", paste(
  "<b>Figure 6a.</b> email-Eu-core, out-degree: empirical complementary",
  "cumulative degree distribution (markers) and the fitted mixed-Poisson",
  "model at the tested null hypothesis (line: pointwise median; band: 95%",
  "envelope over 500 simulated degree sequences of the same size)."),
  "fig6b_openflights_fit.png", "<b>Figure 6b.</b> OpenFlights, out-degree, as in Figure 6a.")
figure("fig6c_celegans_fit.png",
       "<b>Figure 6c.</b> <i>C. elegans</i>, the three degree series, as in Figure 6a.",
       width = 60)
```

## Estimates for the turbulence record

```{r turbulence-data}
turb <- series_table("analyze_turbulence", "Turbulence")
turb$Variant <- ifelse(turb$variant == "full", "full", "thinned")
```

For squared Gaussian velocity increments, the model with $s = 1/2$, $a = 1/2$,
$N = 1$ is exact, so it is the benchmark here. Intervals use a moving-block
bootstrap; the thinned series keep every $k$-th value to reduce serial
dependence.

```{r turbulence-table}
tt <- turb[order(turb$lag, turb$Variant), ]
tab <- show_table(tt, c("lag", "Variant", "n"))
names(tab)[1] <- "Lag (ms)"
knitr::kable(tab, escape = FALSE, align = "rlrcrlrlcr", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r turbulence-plot, fig.cap = "Depth estimates with 95% block-bootstrap intervals for the squared velocity increments, by lag, read from results/analyze_turbulence.json. The dashed line marks the Gaussian benchmark N = 1."}
par_default()
lags <- sort(unique(turb$lag))
plot(NULL, xlim = range(lags) * c(0.8, 1.25), ylim = range(c(turb$N_lo, turb$N_hi)),
     log = "x", xlab = "lag (ms)", ylab = expression(hat(N)), xaxt = "n")
axis(1, at = lags)
abline(h = 1, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
for (j in 1:2) {
  v <- turb[turb$Variant == c("full", "thinned")[j], ]
  v <- v[order(v$lag), ]
  x <- v$lag * c(0.95, 1.05)[j]
  segments(x, v$N_lo, x, v$N_hi, col = pal[j], lwd = 2)
  points(x, v$N_hat, pch = c(16, 17)[j], col = pal[j])
}
legend("bottomleft", bty = "n", col = pal[1:2], pch = c(16, 17), lwd = 2,
       legend = c("full sample", "thinned"))
```

At 2, 5 and 20 ms the test rejects $N = 1$ in the full and the thinned
series, and both intervals for $N$ exclude one: these increments depart from
the Gaussian benchmark. At 10 ms the full series rejects ($p = 0.001$) but the
thinned series does not ($p = 0.254$), and the thinned interval contains one.
At 50 and 100 ms neither series rejects, and the full-sample intervals contain
one; at 100 ms the thinned interval (1.04&ndash;1.43, from 1309 values) does
not. The estimate is not monotone in the lag, and compatibility with $N = 1$
is not the same as Gaussianity.

```{r fig6d}
figure("fig6d_turbulence.png", paste(
  "<b>Figure 6d.</b> p-value of the bootstrap test of H<sub>0</sub>: N = 1",
  "for the squared velocity increments against the lag, for the full sample",
  "and the thinned series; the dashed line marks 0.05."), width = 60)
```

## What the results show and what they do not

- With equal shapes across levels, the class, the shape and the depth of a
  gamma or inverse-gamma cascade are identifiable from the law of the
  innermost temperature, and the same holds for the degrees of the
  hierarchical mixed-Poisson model.
- The depth test holds its level (rejection rates of
  `r sprintf("%.2f", min(rate[, 1]))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(rate[, 1]))`
  under the null) and reaches a power of
  `r sprintf("%.2f", rate[as.character(sizes) == "1000", "2"])` against a
  two-level cascade at $n = 1000$.
- The analysis assumes equal shapes. A cascade with unequal shapes returns an
  effective homogeneous depth.
- No data set here has a known multi-level structure against which an
  estimated depth could be validated. The department labels of email-Eu-core
  are a flat partition, and the geographic levels of OpenFlights were not used
  as a reference.
